messages.author: 2512ced6fd798025
messages.subject: draw a line wtih slope and intercept on an existent ggvis plot
parts:
Just getting start with Shiny. I ask you: is it possible to add single lines characterized by intercept and slope to an existent ggvis plot?  (y= mx+q; m=slope, q=intercept) For example with the package ggplot2 the function to draw a line in a plot is "geom_abline(...)".

I want to add a line over this existent plot: http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/movie-explorer.html

The code of this ggvis plot is in the server.R file located at https://github.com/wch/movies

messages.author: 1161df5ae7a276da
messages.subject: Re: draw a line wtih slope and intercept on an existent ggvis plot
parts:
Hi Davide,

Hadley and Winston, of course, will have the definitive answer, but my best guess is "not yet".

Here's a list of existing analogues between ggplot2 and ggvis: http://ggvis.rstudio.com/layers.html

As a workaround, you could construct a small dataframe with two points that define the line, then add something like layer_lines(data = new_data).

Ian

messages.subject: Re: draw a line wtih slope and intercept on an existent ggvis plot
parts:
Hi Davide

I modified Winston's movie code:

    ### Define a line
    data_line <- data.frame(
      x_rng = c(0, 100), 
      y_rng = c(80, 200)
    )     
    
    movies %>%
      ggvis(x = xvar, y = yvar) %>%
      layer_points(size := 50, size.hover := 200,
        fillOpacity := 0.2, fillOpacity.hover := 0.5,
        stroke = ~has_oscar, key := ~ID) %>%
      ### A couple of ways to display lines
      layer_model_predictions(model = "lm", stroke := "red") %>%
      layer_paths(x = ~x_rng, y = ~y_rng, stroke := "blue", data = data_line) %>%
      ###
      add_tooltip(movie_tooltip, "hover") %>%
      add_axis("x", title = xvar_name) %>%
      add_axis("y", title = yvar_name) %>%
      add_legend("stroke", title = "Won Oscar", values = c("Yes", "No")) %>%
      scale_nominal("stroke", domain = c("Yes", "No"),
        range = c("orange", "#aaa")) %>%
      set_options(width = 500, height = 500)

I know this does not solve the entire ab_line problem - maybe it is enough to make a workaround.

Ian
